verification_report.summary: The unrestricted weighted addition theorem and its corollary are correct under the supplied internal premises, conditional on the exact finite-data existence theorem thm:big-model-exponential audited separately in big_model_measures_01. The weight-truncated data are nonzero finite non-pluripolar measures and yield decreasing solutions. The uniform first moment uses the single fixed reference r=P_theta(u,v); together with the common relative upper bound, it establishes a genuine decreasing L1 limit a in E_phi. Only then is q=P_theta(a,u,v) constructed, so the cutoff argument does not presume a<=u,v. For fixed cutoffs, the right sides converge in total variation against finite input measures. The left sides converge weakly by expanding bounded Omega-psh truncations into positive products with smooth signed factors, applying capacity continuity and locality. Monotone convergence on Borel sets removes the cutoffs without assuming finite undamped weighted mass; the equation then establishes finiteness of the damped sum. Strict domination with constant shifts gives the input order, raw measure bound and uniqueness using finite raw measures. Scaling handles every positive exponent. Injectivity of F_lambda and addition of positive measures establish commutativity, associativity, translation covariance and the diagonal identity even when weighted total masses are infinite. [XL26, Theorem 6.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13446v1) was verified as source attribution only; its conclusion and additional standing global positive-volume hypothesis are not imported. All 15 sequential checks passed; no errors or gaps were found.
